1.why: Every MFA endpoint derives identity solely from the HttpOnly session cookie via authorized(), then looks up users.get(session.userId), so no request-supplied user id can be used and settings always belong to the signed-in account.

2.why: The identity verification code is stored per-session (session.identityCode) and the TOTP secret is per-user encrypted, so a code valid for one user/session cannot authenticate another.

3.why: /api/mfa/activate only flips user.mfa.enabled = true and never iterates the sessions map to revoke other sessions belonging to that user, so any other pre-existing authenticated session remains valid.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as AES-GCM ciphertext (encrypt/encryptedSecret) and backup codes are stored only as salted SHA-256 digests with a per-code 16-byte salt.

5.why: Session ids, CSRF tokens, salts, TOTP secrets, identity codes and recovery codes all come from crypto.getRandomValues, and the AES key from crypto.subtle.generateKey.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used and the only cookie is HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict, though secrets/OTPs/backup codes do live transiently in JS memory and the rendered DOM.

7.why: Server-side regex validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOTP, validRecovery, validCSRF, manualSecret pattern) gate every endpoint, and there is no SQL/database concatenation at all (in-memory Maps).

8.why: All dynamic values inserted into HTML go through the esc() entity-encoder, and a per-response nonce-based CSP (script-src/style-src 'nonce-...') blocks injected inline script.

9.why: The only redirect is a hard-coded 308 to https://localhost:3000/ on the HTTP port with no user-controllable destination parameter, so open redirects are impossible.

10.why: secureHeaders sets HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy, Cache-Control and a CSP with frame-ancestors 'none'; the HTML response gets a stricter nonce CSP.

11.why: cookie()/clearedCookie() emit mfa_session with Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict and a bounded Max-Age.

12.why: Error output is generic with no stack traces and nothing sensitive appears in URLs, but the API returns testIdentityCode/testOtp/secret in responses and the client console.logs the identity code, current OTP and full list of backup recovery codes into a visible logs panel.

13.why: Identity codes expire after 5 minutes and are marked identityUsed, TOTP codes are bound to a 30s counter with verifiedCounter replay prevention, and backup codes are flagged used once consumed.

14.why: Separate failure counters and 5-minute lockouts after MAX_FAILURES = 5 exist for identity, TOTP and recovery attempts, though the counters are per-session rather than per-account, which weakens the control.

15.why: On successful identity verification the old session is deleted and a fresh id/CSRF pair issued, authorized() enforces 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
